comments.content:
I mentioned something very similar on TG and I think it would be better if the standard `manifest.json` contained this info. It could allow external settings validation as opposed to it being bound to inside the plugin because we could take it directly from the manifest.
I think if we are updating the `manifest.json` we should also convert the events into keys so we can dynamically type `SupportedEvents`

You shouldn't have to create a release for this or even your kernel app.
To QA a plugin:
1. run the kernel locally
2. enter this config into your `.ubiquity-os` configuration repo.
```yml
- plugins: 
  - uses:
    - plugin: http:localhost:4000
      with:
        ...plugginSettingsForThisplugin
```
3. run yarn worker inside the plugin repo if it's a worker-friendly plugin.
4. If it's an action plugin, you need to push your changes to the repo and instead of `localhost:4000` you use your repo name so `keyrxng/my-forked-plugin-repo:compute.yml@development` "compute.yml" is our workflow entry do not alter this part, "@dev" is whatever branch you are working on.
5. Trigger a github webhook event which `manifest.json` lists for the plugin and you should see the kernel catch the event in your terminal logs and then it passes it to `localhost:4000` directly to the plugin.
hope this helps

@ishowvel You need to pass in the full webhook name `"pull_request.ready_for_review"` which then gets mapped to it's short name in relation to the timeline.
This [fn](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/blob/9c6380912757547246e780f358431a8242ef6d13/src/types/plugin-input.ts#L39) takes values from this [object](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/blob/9c6380912757547246e780f358431a8242ef6d13/src/types/plugin-input.ts#L27) which contain the full webhook name. This `map.get(webhook)` passes in the full webhook and the `Map` returns the short name.
[This](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-disqualifier/blob/9c6380912757547246e780f358431a8242ef6d13/src/types/plugin-input.ts#L82) is where the schema is validated and rejected if incorrect.
Your TypeBox error is telling you the value that you've placed at the path `/eventWhitelist` which indicates that what you are passing in there doesn't match. 
      'pull_request.review_requested',
      'pull_request.ready_for_review',
      'pull_request_review_comment.created',
      'issue_comment.created',
      'push'
    ],
This is showing you the default values according to the schema had you not passed anything in via the config, these would be used instead.
